reports.note: Several reports of tornado damage around Christiana Hospital. Radar analysis and video confirm a tornado did touch down in this area. More information regarding the tornado will come tomorrow.

NWS Storm Survey found damage consistent with a brief tornado west of Clark in rural southern Randolph County around 10:42 am on Tuesday, November 3rd. The tornado began near the intersection of Route B and County Road 2690, moving to the north northeast where it damaged a farmstead along 2690, inflicting damage to trees and farm outbuildings. The tornado ended near the intersection of County Roads 2690 and D234. The max estimated wind speeds were around 90 mph. The tornado traveled around 1 mile in length, was 50 yards in width, and was on the ground for around 2 minutes.

A tornado carved a narrow southwest-to-northeast path through Keyes, beginning near Phillips Avenue and dissipating past Monroe Avenue. Along the way, it shifted an anchored mobile home, hurled an empty grain silo roughly 100 yards, and snapped utility poles and trees. The most severe destruction occurred near Polk Street, collapsing an old pool hall and tearing the roof and an exterior wall off an adjacent building. Because the majority of the structural damage impacted older, less sturdy buildings, the tornado received a lower rating. Tornado is rated EF1 with max winds rated around 100 mph.
A tornado damaged a home, severely damaged an outbuilding, uprooted numerous trees, and snapped several wooden power poles.

A tornado uprooted numerous trees, snapped the trunks of a couple trees, and snapped numerous large tree limbs. The tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KSRX WSR-88D, and was rated EF-1 based on the damage it produced.
An EF-0 tornado with max wind speed of 85 mph and a path width of 25 yards began at this location. The tornado tracked for 1.10 miles and impacted a barn and RV.
A tornado snapped numerous large tree limbs, moved into terrain that was inaccessible by road, and produced a TDS from the KINX WSR-88D radar.

An EF-0 tornado, with peak winds of 75 mph and a peak width of 150 yards, began just south of Holmes Road in far northwestern DeSoto Parish in a rural and wooded area. It then continued northeastward in a predominantly rural area, crossing into far southwestern Caddo Parish and ending just west of Four Forks Road and south of the Four Forks community. Despite the radar showing a few tornadic debris signatures, the damage was confined to relatively light tree damage with no tree snaps or uproots. The period of the Tornado report was 6 minutes.

An EF-1 tornado began along Old York Road. First noticeable damage was a farm building approximately 3/4 of a mile southwest of the Old York Road and Bordentown Chesterfield Road intersection. All external walls of that building had collapsed. Additional tree damage was noted in multiple locations along Old York Road ahead of the intersection with Bordentown Chesterfield Road. Northeast of the intersection, still along Old York Road, a residence lost a significant portion of the roof over the front of the house. From this point, the tornado continued along a path parallel to Bordentown Chesterfield Road. A school along here lost roof covering and farm equipment nearby was overturned. Some tree damage just beyond the school was the last damage in the continuous path. Estimated maximum wind speed was 100 mph. The total path length was 1.5 miles, and maximum path width was 100 yards.

This EF-0 tornado, with peak winds of 75 mph and a peak width of 50 yards, began near the Texas and Louisiana border to the west of Mooringsport, LA on Parish Road 136 between the Black Bayou and Highway 49. The tornado did mainly tree damage along the roughly one and three-quarter mile track length, ending just to the west of Interstate 49 in Caddo Parish, LA. The period of the Tornado report was 1 minute.

On the afternoon of November 12th, an EF-1 tornado occurred on the eastern side of Newark, in New Castle County, Delaware. The tornado began in the southern portion of the Salem Woods neighborhood traveling to the north-northeast, primarily damaging siding and removing shingles from several houses, as well as uprooting and breaking large branches from a few trees. As the tornado approached White Drive, it began to wrap to the north-northwest, while continuing to produce minor damage to houses along the way. The initial circulation may have briefly lifted here before it touched down again and continued to the northeast where it exited Salem Woods and crossed Old Baltimore Pike into The Oaks neighborhood. Here, more minor roof and siding damage was observed. As the tornado then entered the Timber Farms neighborhood, it likely wrapped up briefly once again near the intersection of Hummock Lane and Marie Court. A very brief tornado moved across a farmstead approximately 5 miles northeast of Madison, resulting in a broken tree and other minor tree damage.

This tornado developed south of Big Sky Lane and east of the S 4060 Road. It moved northeast, crossing Big Sky Lane and the E 360 Road, snapping numerous large tree limbs before moving into open terrain. The tornado dissipated south of the E 340 Road. It produced a tornadic debris signature from the KINX WSR-88D radar, and was likely more intense north of the E 360 Road (based on radar data), but any damage in that part of the path was inaccessible by road, and therefore, couldn't be assessed.

This tornado developed south of the E 390 Road and east of the N 435 Road. It moved north-northeast across the E 390 Road, where numerous trees were uprooted, and a home and outbuilding were damaged. The tornado then moved through open terrain that was inaccessible by road for about a mile and a half. It then snapped several power poles south of the E 370 Road, uprooted trees along the E 370 Road and S 4360 Road, and dissipated south of the E 360 Road. The tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KINX WSR-88D.

Around 10:17am on November 3rd, 2026, a mini supercell developed out ahead of a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) near the Texas and Louisiana border to the west of Mooringsport, LA. This mini supercell produced a very brief EF-0 tornado that touched down on Parish Road 136 between the Black Bayou and Highway 49. The tornado downed a large hardwood tree along this Parish Road as it then continued northeast towards Highway 49. Before the tornado reached Highway 49, it moved across the intersection of Parish Road 136 and Gamm Road, where a storm spotter captured a geotagged photo of the tornado lifting just west of Highway 49.  The storm survey team consulted numerous residents, law enforcement officials, and utility workers to help determine whether the tornado track continued beyond Highway 49 after witnessing a lack of additional damage, and these conversations led the team to conclude that there was no additional damage from this storm. This weak tornado, originating from a quasi-linear convective system, began just south of Holmes Road in far northwestern DeSoto Parish in a rural and wooded area. It then continued northeastward in a predominantly rural area, crossing into far southwestern Caddo Parish and ending just west of Four Forks Road and south of the Four Forks community.  Despite the radar showing a few tornadic debris signatures, the damage was confined to relatively light tree damage with no tree snaps or uproots. This limited the survey team's rating to an EF-0.

This same thunderstorm line segment advanced northeast, prompting a few tornado warnings in Shreveport and Bossier City. A tornadic debris signature was noted near Bert Kouns Road, approximately 3 miles south-southeast of the Shreveport Airport.  However, the NWS survey team could not find ratable damage there. This tornado developed over rugged terrain west of Cedarville on a ridgetop. It moved north-northeast across Rocky Road and Shiloh Road, where trees were uprooted and a few were snapped, and numerous large tree limbs were snapped. The tornado then moved northeast through rugged terrain after crossing Broken Trail, and then uprooted a few trees and snapped large tree limbs along Creekside Way and finally on Highway 59 before dissipating. The tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KSRX WSR-88D.

Chaser video showed the circulation was on the ground west of Singhurst Street before it crossed the street and partially destroyed a barn and pushed an RV off its foundation. The tornado then continued through tree groves but caused no additional damage. Chaser footage showed the circulation was still in contact with the ground as far east as State Road 159.
